  \caption{\textbf{Bayesian MVT captures patch-leaving behavior and manipulations.}
    (\subref{fig:2-a}) MVT schematic: optimal forager leaves when local reward rate falls below global average set by travel costs.
    (\subref{fig:2-b}) Depletion curves for High (orange, $p_0=0.9$) and Low (teal, $p_0=0.6$) patches; MVT predicts a common leaving threshold (dashed).
    (\subref{fig:2-c}) Bayesian MVT model: odor-cued posteriors over $q$ updated with forgetting $\delta < 1$; agent leaves when sampled local rate falls below $\bar{R}$.
    (\subref{fig:2-d}) Six leaving metrics for mice ($N=24$): $P(\text{reward})$ at leaving does not differ across patch types (n.s.); all other metrics differ ($^{***}p<0.001$).
    (\subref{fig:2-e}) Model reproduces all six metrics.
    (\subref{fig:2-f}) Change in $P(\text{reward})$ at leaving vs.\ inter-patch distance in mice.
    (\subref{fig:2-g}) Same for model simulations.
    (\subref{fig:2-h}) \emph{Placeholder}: PCA trajectories of population activity separating task epochs and patch type.
    (\subref{fig:2-i}) \emph{Placeholder}: population-average PSTHs aligned to odor onset showing heterogeneous functional cell types.}
